column4: The broken gloss "pertaining" points to a sense already covered by the other listed meanings (real, realistic, real numbers, inflation-corrected), so this entry only duplicates them.
Hollander as an adjective is nonstandard and rare; learners should use the adjective Hollands, so this meaning only confuses.
This wreath-of-roses sense is archaic and obscure, and the gloss "less commonly" is not a translation; the common rosary meaning is already listed.
The adjective 'marker' does not mean 'of' in Dutch, so this meaning does not exist for the word.
The only other meaning is 'Persian', which this item duplicates, and the gloss 'in' is not a valid translation.
This is not a standard, reliably attested adjective with a clear meaning, so it would only confuse a learner.
In particular is an adverb that does not translate this noun, and the real meanings (bungler, tradesman) are already listed, so this entry adds only confusion.
Hence metaphorically is not a translation, and the only real meaning, purse-snatcher, is already listed as another meaning, so this is a duplicate.
Of is not a translation, and the only real meaning, experiential, is already listed, while the word is obscure religious jargon that would only confuse a learner.
The meaning "Corsican" is already listed as another meaning, so this item duplicates it and the gloss "in" is wrong.
This archaic, obscure adjective only confuses learners, so it should be removed.
The gloss 'in' is wrong, and the only other meaning, 'Faroese', is the same as this meaning, so the entry duplicates itself.
The gloss "in" is wrong, and this meaning duplicates the separate Greenlandic meaning already listed for the word.
This archaic adjective form only confuses learners, since "Haarlems" is the normal form for this meaning.
The meaning "Icelandic" is already listed as another meaning, so this entry duplicates it and the gloss "in" is wrong.
This is an archaic place-derived adjective (from Krimpen) that is obscure and would only confuse a learner.
The meaning is simply Laotian, which duplicates the listed other meaning, and the gloss "in" is wrong.
The literal mastodon sense is already listed under other meanings, and the gloss "someone" matches no real sense of this word, so this entry duplicates and confuses.
Taalpolitiek is a feminine noun meaning language policy and has no adjective meaning, so this entry does not exist.
'Tweede garnituur' is a rare, obscure term (a second set of staff or spare equipment), and the gloss 'someone' is simply wrong, so the entry only confuses learners.
Veers is an obscure, archaic or dialect form with no reliable modern meaning, so it would only confuse a learner.
The "being worn" sense is just the "on" meaning of aan already listed, so it duplicates another meaning, and the given example belongs to a different word sense (aanstellen).
Denoting growth is not a meaning of the adverb aan; the example uses aan as a prepositional complement of bijdragen, so the meaning does not exist for this word class.
The 'adjust' sense only exists within the separable verb bijstellen, not as a standalone meaning of bij, so learners should look up the verb instead.
During is not a real standalone meaning of onder; the example clearly shows the "under" sense, so this entry only confuses learners.
This archaic sense ('to receive priority') is obscure, the gloss 'to wage war' is wrong for the example, and the meaning largely duplicates 'to get'.
The call sense belongs to the word telefoontje, and the word telefoon is already covered by the telephone (device) meaning.
The 'rid of' sense only appears in the idiom 'ervan af willen' and duplicates the 'away from' meaning, so it only confuses learners as a standalone preposition meaning.
'Movie sector' is not a separate meaning for this word; the industry sense duplicates the 'film; film production' meaning and the example shows the ordinary film sense.
'Upset' is a mistranslation of 'boos', and this entry duplicates the angry meaning already covered by item 3.
The meaning 'intelligent' duplicates the other listed meaning 'clever', so it should be removed to avoid a redundant entry.
Relationship and "relation" are the same meaning, so this entry duplicates the other listed meaning.
Je van het is not an established Dutch expression, and the example is unnatural, so this entry would only confuse a learner.
De wel meaning spring or well is rare and literary, so it is too obscure for learners and only adds confusion.
The meaning shown in the example, 'all through/throughout' a period of time, duplicates the listed 'throughout' meaning, and 'through' does not fit it.
Yet again is essentially the same meaning as "once again", so this entry duplicates another meaning and only confuses learners.
The noun "de weer" meaning defence is archaic, the example actually uses the phrase "te weer" rather than this noun, and the listed meanings are obscure, so this entry only confuses learners.
It is a duplicate of item 2 with the same meaning, so it only repeats the entry.
Adjective "af" does not mean "out" in this sense, and its real sense of "finished" is already listed as the other meaning, so this entry only confuses.
Te is not an article; it is an infinitive marker or the adverb 'too', and the 'in idiom' meaning is not a real meaning of this word.
Binnen has no adjective meaning 'set for life'; it is a preposition or adverb meaning 'inside' or 'within', so this entry is invalid.
'Plus' is just the arithmetic use of the conjunction 'and', so it duplicates the 'and' meaning rather than being a separate meaning.
Adverbial 'van' meaning 'from' appears only in fixed forms like 'vandaan' and 'vanaf', and it duplicates the 'from' sense already listed for the preposition.
This conjunction meaning is just 'but', which duplicates the listed 'but; yet' meaning, and 'but then' is unnatural.
The weather use is just the impersonal 'het is' construction of 'to be', which is already listed as another meaning, so it duplicates it.
'De wel' is an archaic or poetic noun whose main sense 'well' duplicates the listed other meaning, and 'shaft' is not a valid gloss.
De nu is not a valid noun; the Dutch noun for "the present" is "het nu", which duplicates the existing "present" meaning.
Wie as a noun is not a standard meaning; the word is a question pronoun meaning "who", so this entry only confuses learners.
This archaic meaning of door as a noun for fool is obscure and would only confuse a learner.
Callus is not a live meaning of 'weer'; it is an obscure, archaic sense that would only confuse a learner, and the gender pairing with 'het' is unsupported.
'Foxing' in textiles is a highly specialized, obscure sense not used in everyday Dutch and would only confuse a learner.
'Knot in wood' is an obscure, dialectal or archaic sense that is not a standard modern meaning of 'weer'.
'De weer' is not standard Dutch, and 'resistance' is an archaic sense whose modern equivalent is 'weerstand', so this entry only misleads.
'Seisin' is an obscure legal term from English property law with no real modern Dutch use of 'de weer', so it only confuses learners.
The gloss "wether" (a castrated ram) belongs to a different word, and the real meaning of "weer" is already covered by "weather" in the other meanings, so this entry only duplicates and confuses.
Z is an abbreviation or letter for "zuid" and is not an adverb, so this meaning does not exist for the word.
Confirmed is not a meaning of "zeker", and the real senses (certain, confident) are already listed, so this entry is wrong and duplicates.
Dag does not mean meeting; that meaning is wrong and would mislead learners.
The rope sense is not a real standard Dutch meaning of dag and is too obscure to help learners.
Na as an adjective meaning close is not a valid meaning; close is nabij or dichtbij.
Broken up is the same meaning as the listed split up and separated, so it is a duplicate.
The gloss "separated" duplicates the listed meaning "split up; broken up" for the same relationship sense, so this entry adds nothing new.
Clear is not a meaning of klaar; the sense of clarity is covered by "helder" or "duidelijk", and the "obvious" sense is already listed.
Helemaal does not mean "especially"; its real senses, "completely" and "anyway", are already listed, so this entry is wrong and redundant.
Horse tackle is not a real meaning of 'want'; its real senses are mitten and rigging, which are already listed.
'Cowl on a chimney' is not a meaning of 'gek', which is a noun meaning lunatic (already listed), so this sense does not exist.
'Bang' is an adjective meaning afraid, not a noun, so the noun meaning 'sharp' does not exist.
'O' has no adjective meaning 'neutral'; it is only an interjection or letter, so this entry is invalid.
o is an abbreviation of "oost", not an adverb meaning east, so this entry only confuses a learner.
het heen is not a real noun meaning sea clubrush; it is an obscure, incorrect entry that would mislead a learner.
The "mass" sense duplicates the existing pile and multitude meanings of "de hoop", so it should be removed.
